newsitem.title: UK: Softs outlook - Coffee seeks a low profile.
newsitem.headline: Softs outlook - Coffee seeks a low profile.

text.p: Coffee will try to keep a low profile after last week's stormy ride but it will stay on guard for any crop news that may revive the rally, traders said on Monday.

"The market is still extremely jumpy. I don't think any coffee broker or trader is going to put their house on where prices are going to go because the market is very thin at times," said one in London.
"It's a very frightening market to trade."

London's well-supplied robusta market is already limping, with Indonesian crops preparing to hit the world market next month, but players may still be tempted this week by New York's upward aspirations.
They will mull a revised estimate by private consultant Leon Yallouz who was said on Friday to have revised down the 1997/98 Brazilian crop estimate to above 25 million 60-kg bags.
Other traders in Brazil said they had heard the latest forecast was in the region of 27.5 million bags, compared with producers' estimates of around 20 million.
The higher end of forecasts support the view that the market, which has soared 55 percent in New York since the beginning of the year, has seen its peak.
Friday's CFTC Commitment of Traders Report showed again a large total net speculative long position of 14,034 lots, keeping the market prone to a selling bout.
In cocoa, the March structure could continue to tighten as shorts cover positions, inviting players to speculate about possible manoeuverings by one trade house which controls large physical stocks.
Friday's close below 890 stg per tonne on May dashed hopes for a continued rally to excite the shorts. May made some upwards progress last week but reversed twice from a peak of 898 stg.
"At the moment it's hit or miss. One weak close and that's it, game over. All optimism can go straight out the window," said one trader.
But last week's overall gains, which set a higher trading ground on the charts, may have wiped off any complacency among shorts, traders said.
The CFTC report showed, as expected, speculators were still net short of the market in New York.

In white sugar, London should see a new lease on life this week now that the New York raws expiry is out of the way, as much of traders' attention has been centred on rolling out of the spot March contract.

Traders said a corrective slide was expected on the raws, with the whites likely to follow suit, but the different paces of decline could cause May/May to widen. The arbitrage fluctuated between $65 and $68 last week.

"Technically, it (New York) might drop a little bit and we'll take it from there once we fall through the retracement and force the funds out -- and London will follow on from there," said one trader.

Analysts pegged support at between $303 and $304 but said values appeared content to hover between support and $310. Support would remain intact provided May held above an upward trendline dating from mid-January, they said.
"It's quite traditional when you have expiries quite close together we tend to get this quiet period in London," said another trader.
